input.eventDetails: First one since I started the job three weeks ago. Mostly people from other teams I have not met.
input.people: My manager will be there, plus people from departments I do not work with.
input.concerns: I am not sure how much to talk about myself since I am still new.

output.what_to_aim_for: Leave having had a few short conversations with people you did not know before — not dazzling anyone, just making yourself a recognizable face. Three weeks in, showing up and being pleasant is the whole job.
simple_plan: Pick one person standing alone or on the edge of a group and introduce yourself by name and team — that is enough to start
Ask questions about what they work on and let the conversation run on their answers rather than filling silence with your own story
When a conversation winds down naturally, use it — say it was good to meet them and move on rather than holding on past its natural end

starters.use_when: You are near someone you have not met and want a simple, honest opener
starters.say: Hey — I am [your name], I just joined the [your team] team about three weeks ago. I do not think we have crossed paths yet.
starters.why_it_helps: It gives them your name and context immediately, and the 'three weeks' detail invites them to orient you without requiring you to pitch yourself

starters.use_when: You have exchanged names and need somewhere to go next
starters.say: What does your team actually handle day to day — I am still piecing together how everything connects here.
starters.why_it_helps: It gives them a specific, easy question to answer, and your stated reason for asking makes it feel natural rather than interrogative

starters.use_when: The conversation has reached a natural pause and you want to move on cleanly
starters.say: Really good to finally meet some people from other teams — I will let you get back to it.
starters.why_it_helps: It closes warmly without requiring a manufactured reason to leave, and the word 'finally' frames your presence at the event as intentional

if_it_stalls.try: Redirect toward something in the room or the event rather than pushing back into the conversation
if_it_stalls.say: I am going to grab a drink — good meeting you though.

things_to_handle_carefully: Your manager is in the room — keep the tone social rather than work-update mode, since this is a happy hour, not a check-in
You do not need to volunteer a lot about your role or impressions so far — at three weeks in, listening reads better than having strong opinions
output.one_thing_to_remember: You control whether you show up, say hello, and ask a genuine question — everything after that can take care of itself.

input.whatYouSaid: I told my coworker her presentation was interesting when I actually thought it was confusing and too long.
input.context: Right after the meeting, in front of two other people

output.what_happened: You told a coworker her presentation was interesting immediately after a meeting, in front of two colleagues, when you actually found it confusing and too long.

do_you_need_to_fix_it.why: Saying something was 'interesting' is vague enough that it reads as a polite acknowledgment rather than a false claim. Whether you need to address it depends on whether the coworker reacted—did she seem to notice the mismatch, push back, or let it pass?

output.or_just_keep_going: A mild, face-saving comment after a meeting is ordinary social behavior. If the moment passed without friction, nothing requires you to revisit it now.
output.if_they_reacted_badly: If she asks what specifically interested you or seems dissatisfied with your response, you could say 'I think I need to sit with it more—there was a lot to take in,' which is honest and does not require you to litigate your real reaction on the spot.

input.theyDid: My friend has been replying to my texts with one word answers for the past week, but she liked my last Instagram post.
input.context: We usually text a lot back and forth
input.yourConcern: Did I do something to upset her?

my_read.label: several plausible reads
my_read.explanation: The one-word texts suggest something has shifted, but the Instagram like is a small signal of continued goodwill that makes a clean falling-out less certain.

what_supports_that_read: One-word replies over a full week is a noticeable departure from your usual back-and-forth pattern
The change is sustained, not a one-off busy day
The Instagram like shows she is seeing your content and choosing to engage, at least passively
other_plausible_reads: She is going through something personally — stress, low mood, family trouble — that has drained her capacity for conversation broadly, not just with you
Something you said or did landed wrong, and she is pulling back without having said so
She is in a phase of generally reducing screen time or texting, and the Instagram like slipped through out of habit
what_this_does_not_tell_you: Whether this is about you specifically or about something in her own life
Whether she is aware the shift is noticeable
How she would respond if you named it directly
what_to_watch_next: Whether she initiates anything — a text, a reaction, a comment — in the next few days without you prompting her
Whether her replies get shorter still or start to lengthen again on their own
output.what_to_do_now: Send one low-pressure check-in — something like 'Hey, just wanted to see how you're doing' — that opens a door without putting her on the spot, and see what comes back.
